name: site-footer
description: The end of the page, and the answer to "a page ends on purpose". One slot and no parts previously, while the real footer carried a brand block, three separate link groups each with its own heading, and a legal line — assembled by hand in one component. Three `<nav>` elements is correct and needs three labels; without them a screen reader hears "navigation" three times and cannot tell which is which.

base.$description:
CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

`inline-size: 100%` is the container's REQUIRED companion, not a preference. `container-type: inline-size` makes the box's width independent of its contents — that is the containment being asked for — so a container with no width of its own has nothing left to size from and collapses to zero. This unit did: centred in a grid it became a column of single words. A container fills what it is given and bounds itself with `max-inline-size`; it never sizes to its text.

An explicit `display`, and it is load-bearing rather than tidy. `container-type: inline-size` has NO EFFECT on an element whose display is `inline` — containment needs a block box. This unit declared no display, so rendered as a `<span>` it was `inline`, its containment was inert, and every `@container` rule inside it silently never matched. The navbar found it: at 318px it was still showing a full desktop nav because the query it was waiting on could not fire.

inner.$description: IT PADS ITSELF. `max-inline-size` alone caps the measure but does nothing at any viewport narrower than the cap, where the content simply touches the edge. Every call site was left to supply that padding and they did it differently — the website's footer spells it `px-5 sm:px-8` — which is exactly the restatement this actor exists to remove.

groups.$description: `auto-fit` with a `minmax` floor rather than a column count, so three groups become two and then one without a breakpoint per step.

group-title.$description: Composes `text--eyebrow`. Only the colour is this unit's; the size, weight, case and tracking come from the one definition.

meta.$description: The legal line. Wraps to a column on a narrow viewport rather than shrinking a copyright notice past its own words.

page.$description: For a surface whose page is already dark, where a marine footer would vanish into it.

a11y.note: Each link group is its own `<nav>` with its own `aria-label` — "Product", "Legal", "Social" — because three unlabelled navigation landmarks in one footer tell a screen-reader user nothing about which is which. The footer is a `contentinfo` landmark by virtue of being a top-level `<footer>`, and stops being one if it is nested inside a `<section>`.
